newsitem.title: USA: Alcoa earnings hurt by strike, aluminum contracts.
newsitem.headline: Alcoa earnings hurt by strike, aluminum contracts.

text.p: Aluminum Co. of America said Friday it earned $68 million in its third quarter as a strike at a forging plant contributed to a 70 percent drop from its profit a year earlier.
Alcoa, the world's largest producer of aluminum, said it earned 39 cents a share on sales of $3.2 billion. A year earlier, the company earned $226 million, or $1.27 a share, on sales of $3.3 billion.
Alcoa said its operating income was 77 cents a share, which compared with the 95 cents that Wall Street analysts had expected.
The results touched off heavy selling in Alcoa's stock and its stock was down 87.5 cents at $59.50 after falling as low as $57.125 on the New York Stock Exchange.

"This is the kind of market that has no interest in companies without earnings momentum," said Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co. "The pressure is for short-term performance."

Alcoa said a strike at a forging plant in Cleveland hurt earnings by $6.5 million. In addition, the company posted a loss of $16 million as a result of accounting procedures related to certain aluminum commodity contracts.
Alcoa also took a one-time charge of $65.5 million, or 38 cents a share, as a result of layoffs and equipment write-downs it announced previously.
The company said the results reflect lower realised prices for aluminum ingot and fabricated products including rigid container sheet and also higher costs for raw materials.
